description: Eight secondary-electron SEM micrographs (a)–(h) of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel annealed 1 h at 700, 800, 850, 900, 950, 1000, 1100 and 1200 °C, each labelled top-right with its temperature and time. Scale bars: 10 µm in (a) and (b), 20 µm in (c)–(e), 50 µm in (f) and (g), 150 µm in (h). Panel (a) carries TD/RD axis arrows (RD–TD section) and shows a dark featureless α region together with a large α+κ area of fine lamellar/rod-like κ-carbide in α matrix, with a white "κ" tag at a cusp and a white "α" tag; (b) adds a blue "γ" tag, and its κ-carbide is visibly coarser and more globular; (c) at 850 °C shows more γ and less κ. In (d)–(g) (900–1100 °C) no κ-carbide is resolvable in the matrix and α and γ grains coarsen; red arrows mark small α grains inside γ regions. (h) is the RD–ND section (ND/RD arrows) at 1200 °C, showing a banded structure with blue "γ" and red "α" tags. Together the panels demonstrate the γ → α + κ eutectoid decomposition, κ-carbide coarsening then dissolution between 850 and 900 °C, and continuous grain growth of α and γ up to 1200 °C.

observations.observation: Panels are SEM micrographs, each carrying a top-right label of annealing temperature and time: 700 °C, 1 h (a); 800 °C, 1 h (b); 850 °C, 1 h (c); 900 °C, 1 h (d); 950 °C, 1 h (e); 1000 °C, 1 h (f); 1100 °C, 1 h (g); 1200 °C, 1 h (h).
Scale bars are printed as 10 µm in (a) and (b), 20 µm in (c), (d) and (e), 50 µm in (f) and (g), and 150 µm in (h).

Panel (a) shows dark featureless 'α' regions coexisting with an extensive 'α+κ' region in which fine lamellar/rod-like second phase lies in the α matrix; a white 'κ' tag with an arrow marks one such feature at a boundary cusp.
Panel (a) has TD (up) and RD (right) axis arrows indicating the RD–TD section; panel (h) has ND (up) and RD (right) axis arrows indicating the RD–ND section.
Panel (b) additionally contains a blue 'γ' label marking an austenite region, and its κ-carbide appears coarser and closer to globular than that in (a).
In panels (d) through (g) (900–1100 °C) no κ-carbide is resolvable in the matrix; only α and γ grains with an increasing grain size are seen.
Red arrows in panels (d), (e), (f) and (g) point to small α grains located among γ grains.
The caption states that (a) through (g) show the microstructures of the RD–TD section, while (h) shows the RD–ND section of the specimen.
The citing text states that after annealing at 700 °C the γ phase has almost decomposed into lamellar κ-carbide and α matrix by the eutectoid reaction γ → α + κ.
The citing text states that, compared with the 700 °C specimen, κ-carbide in the 800 °C specimen is larger, its fraction is lower and its shape is closer to globular.

The citing text states that the γ phase volume fraction is about 29% at 800 °C and about 39% at 850 °C, and that the γ fraction increases while κ-carbide and α fractions decrease as annealing temperature rises from 700 °C to 900 °C.
The citing text states that the dissolution temperature of κ-carbide lies between 850 °C and 900 °C, so κ-carbide dissolves when the annealing temperature reaches 900 °C.

The citing text states that in the specimen annealed at 1200 °C there are needle-shaped or plate-shaped particles in some large α grains (Fig. 6(h) and Fig. 10(d)); these particles are not clearly resolvable in the supplied image of panel (h).
The citing text states that the banded structure becomes less contiguous at higher annealing temperatures, as seen in panels (a), (c) and (h).
The citing text states that the average grain sizes of the phases increase with annealing temperature from 900 °C to 1200 °C, measured from SEM micrographs (reported in Fig. 9).

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph, 700 °C, 1 h, 10 µm scale bar, RD–TD section with TD/RD axis arrows. Dark featureless α region and an extensive α+κ region of fine lamellar/rod-like κ-carbide in α matrix; white tags 'κ' (arrow at a boundary cusp), 'α' and blue 'α+κ'.

SEM micrograph, 800 °C, 1 h, 10 µm scale bar. Large dark α field at top, rod-like/globular κ-carbide (white 'κ' tag, orange arrow) and blue 'α+κ' label, plus a blue 'γ' label in the lower-left; κ-carbide appears coarser and more globular than in (a).
SEM micrograph, 850 °C, 1 h, 20 µm scale bar. Increased γ fraction (blue 'γ' tag) with reduced, finer κ-carbide along boundaries (white 'κ' tag with arrow) and α regions (white 'α' tag).
SEM micrograph, 900 °C, 1 h, 20 µm scale bar. Large continuous α band (white 'α') plus γ grains (blue 'γ') with a red arrow to a small α grain among γ; no obvious κ-carbide resolvable in the matrix.
SEM micrograph, 950 °C, 1 h, 20 µm scale bar. α grain (white 'α') and γ region (blue 'γ') with red arrow marking a small α grain; grain boundaries clearly outlined, no matrix κ-carbide visible.
SEM micrograph, 1000 °C, 1 h, 50 µm scale bar. Coarse α grains (white 'α', plus red-arrowed α) and γ (blue 'γ'); matrix free of resolvable κ-carbide.
SEM micrograph, 1100 °C, 1 h, 50 µm scale bar. Further coarsened α (white 'α', red-arrowed α) and γ (blue 'γ') grains with wavy boundaries.

SEM micrograph, 1200 °C, 1 h, 150 µm scale bar, ND–RD section (ND/RD axis arrows). Banded structure of elongated light bands in a darker matrix with equiaxed grain boundaries; blue arrow labelled 'γ' and red arrow labelled 'α'.

unreadable_items: panel (h): needle-/plate-like particles inside large α grains, asserted in the citing text, are not clearly resolvable at the supplied resolution
panels (d)–(g): small dark speckles/dots present within grains (possibly boundary κ-carbide or artefacts) are too small to identify
panel (h): individual grain boundaries within the light bands are partially indistinct at the printed scale
